slides.title: Coffee has a season, like fruit
slides.subtitle: So why does the shelf look the same all year?

slides.myth: Coffee is a pantry staple with no season.
slides.truth: Coffee beans are the seeds of a fruit, the coffee cherry. In most growing countries, the cherries are picked once a year, when they ripen. Some places get a smaller second harvest.

right.label: Central America
points: Harvest from late fall to early spring

slides.title: Why the shelf never looks empty
slides.body: Different countries pick at different times, so there is always a recent harvest somewhere. Roasters buy from several origins and change their lineup through the year. Green coffee, the raw unroasted bean, keeps for months, but not forever.
slides.highlight: Seasonal coffees come and go, like fruit.

slides.label: The tip
slides.body: Some bags print the harvest year next to the roast date. If yours does, a recent harvest is a good sign. If not, ask the roaster.

slides.title: Coffee is a crop, not a constant
slides.body: Picked once a year in most places, so harvests come and go like fruit.
